timelines.title: Envelope - Front
timelines.description: Explore the front of a pattern envelope to identify the garment design, available views, style variations, and finished garment examples.

timelines.title: Envelope - Back
timelines.description: Learn how to read the size chart and body measurement guide on the back of a pattern envelope to find the size that best matches your measurements.

timelines.title: Body vs. Finished Garment Measurements
timelines.description: Understand the difference between your body measurements and the finished garment measurements. The difference, known as ease, affects how comfortably and loosely a garment fits.

timelines.title: Envelope Back - Garment Details
timelines.description: Read the garment description to understand the design features, included views, and construction details before choosing a pattern.

timelines.title: English & Imperial / French & Metric
timelines.description: Learn how to read fabric requirements, yardage, and notions in different measurement systems. Check the correct units and quantities for your chosen size and view.

timelines.title: Pattern Instructions
timelines.description: Explore the instruction booklet to understand the sewing steps, pattern piece references, and cutting layouts that show how to arrange the pieces on your fabric.

timelines.title: Paper Pattern
timelines.description: Learn how to identify individual paper pattern pieces, cutting lines for different sizes, and grainline arrows that guide correct placement on the fabric.

timelines.title: Triangles = Notches
timelines.description: Recognize triangle-shaped notches and other common pattern markings. These marks help you align pattern pieces and identify important construction details.

timelines.title: Physical Patterns
timelines.description:
Ready to Use: Printed pattern pieces are supplied on paper, so you can start preparing your project without printing or assembling pages.
No Printing or Taping: The pattern pieces are already printed. Select your size and transfer any necessary markings before cutting the fabric.
Store and Reuse: Keep the pattern pieces and instructions together in their envelope. Store them carefully to prevent damage and reuse them for future projects.

timelines.title: PDF Patterns
timelines.description:
Instant Download: Download the digital pattern file to your computer or tablet and access it whenever you need.
Print at Home or at a Copy Shop: Print tiled patterns on A4 or US Letter paper and assemble the pages, or use a copy shop for large-format printing such as A0.
Convenient & Flexible: Store the file digitally and print another copy when needed. Always select Actual Size or 100% scale and check the test square to ensure the pattern prints at the correct size.

timelines.title: Print at Home — A4 / US Letter
timelines.description:
Print at Home: The pattern is divided into multiple A4 or US Letter pages. Print the pages, trim the margins, and tape them together using the numbered guides, like assembling a puzzle.
Check the Print Scale: Select Actual Size or 100% scale instead of Fit to Page. Measure the test square, if provided, to make sure the pattern prints at the correct size.
Assemble the Pattern: Align the numbered guides and matching marks carefully before taping the pages together. Check that the pattern lines connect correctly across the sheets.

timelines.title: Large-Format / Copyshop Printing — A0
timelines.description:
Print on Large Sheets: The pattern is printed on one to three large A0 sheets, depending on the pattern layout, without needing to tape multiple pages together.
Choose a Copy Shop: Send the A0 pattern file to a print shop that handles technical or architectural drawings. Confirm that the shop can print the required paper size.
Check the Printed Pattern: Make sure the print scale is correct and that the pattern dimensions match the original file before cutting the pieces out.

timelines.title: Projector Sewing
timelines.description:
Project Directly onto Fabric: Use a ceiling-mounted projector to display the digital pattern directly onto the fabric, eliminating the need for printed paper.
Calibrate the Projector: Adjust the projector position and zoom until the pattern appears at the correct scale. Use the pattern's test square or measurement guide to verify accuracy.
Trace and Cut: Align the projected pattern with the fabric grain, select the correct size, and mark or cut the fabric according to the pattern instructions.
